title: Reuse validated coordinate labels for TensorView canonical ordering
masterplan_authority: Revision 11 / Version 2.2.0 / Gate 1 — Renovation and owner-directed Genesis
finding: TensorView validates every entry coordinate label against a canonically sorted TensorAxis before sorting and retaining entries, but its canonical entry-order key converted every validated label back to its numeric axis position with bisect_left. Construction paid that conversion for every sort-key evaluation, and index_coordinate()/prefix select repeated the same label-position reconstruction during binary-search comparisons. The numeric position is required only by the public index_coordinate() result, not to preserve canonical ordering.
primary_claim: TensorView now orders and bisects entries directly by the already-validated canonical coordinate tuples. Because each TensorAxis.labels sequence is canonical lexicographic order and every retained coordinate was validated against that axis, coordinate-label order is order-isomorphic to the former numeric label-position order. index_coordinate() converts labels to integer positions only after exact retained-entry equality is established; prefix select bisects the same canonical coordinate tuples directly.
gardener_decision: Reuse the canonical coordinate representation already owned and validated by SparseTensorEntry/TensorView rather than rebuilding numeric label-position tuples inside entry-order comparisons or introducing an entry-key cache/index. Keep numeric projection only at the API boundary that actually returns integer coordinates.
acceptance: construction sorts retained entries by the existing validated canonical coordinate tuple while preserving relation/masked/value/evidence tie-breakers
index_coordinate bisects retained entries without rereading axis labels during entry comparisons and projects to integer label positions only after exact retained-entry equality
prefix select validates its requested label once and bisects canonical coordinate tuples without repeatedly reconstructing numeric label positions
an adversarial 512-entry label-read probe caps node-label reads at 16, observes zero plane-label reads for the node-prefix selection, and keeps final index projection bounded
existing binary-entry-read, non-prefix filtering, unknown-axis/label and foreign-entry fail-closed regressions remain in the focused contract surface
